interpretations: Filter on results.grid > 12 (strictly greater, so grids 13 and up). Group by driver across all their races. Per driver, SUM(points) and AVG(laps, with laps cast to a number and NULLs ignored). Then average the per-driver point totals and the per-driver average laps (AVG of AVG).
Same as 1, but the filter is grid >= 12 ("upwards of 12" read as inclusive).
Same as 1, but group by driverId, so drivers with the same name count as separate drivers. Or group by driver name (forename and surname), which would merge any drivers sharing a name.

Same as 1, but treat each driver-race result row as the unit, with no per-driver grouping. That gives the average points per row and the average laps per row. This ignores the "add up each driver's points" part, so it is less likely.
Same as 1, but group by driver and constructor, or by driver and season. Points would then be totalled per driver-constructor or per driver-year pair before averaging.
Same as 1, but the average of averages is weighted by each driver's number of qualifying races rather than being a simple mean across drivers.

Same as 1, but with laps treated as text. This means laps may need a numeric cast, and values such as "\N" or empty strings are treated as missing and excluded. Alternatively, laps stored as text could be averaged without a cast, which in SQLite still coerces numeric strings.
Same as 1, but grid = 0 (pit-lane starts) is excluded or included. Under "upwards of 12" it is naturally excluded, so only grid values above 12 count.
Same as 1, but drivers with a NULL points value in every qualifying row are excluded from the points average, or their SUM is treated as 0 and they are kept.
The output is a single row with two columns: the average of the per-driver point totals and the average of the per-driver average laps, both unrounded.
Same as 1, but the AVG of laps is taken over all rows, including those whose laps are NULL or "\N", with those values coerced to 0 rather than ignored.
Same as 1, but the final average of per-driver point totals is computed over only the drivers with a non-zero total, which excludes drivers who scored no points from the grid > 12 rows.
Same as 1, but "average of their average laps" is a pooled average, meaning total laps divided by total rows across all qualifying results, not an average of per-driver averages.
Same as 1, but the grid filter is applied after joining to races, restricted to particular seasons or to races that have a driver-standings record.
Same as 1, but points are taken from driverStandings, which are running totals, instead of results.points.
